title: Slider
wrapsNative: Slider(value:in:step:) for the system control; the example draws the track and ring thumb of the web from the theme (a Capsule track, a ring Circle and a DragGesture), because SwiftUI has no style API for Slider
summary: One number on a track uses the standard Slider. Inside a Monarch theme the filled part of the track takes the accent from the tint. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a value where the position matters more than the exact number, such as volume or a share.
whenNotToUse: For an exact number use a text field or a Stepper. For a rating use MonarchRatingPicker. For two thumbs use MonarchRangeSlider.
api: Slider(value: Binding<V>, in: ClosedRange<V>, step: V.Stride, label: () -> Label, minimumValueLabel: () -> ValueLabel, maximumValueLabel: () -> ValueLabel, onEditingChanged: (Bool) -> Void)

states.name: value
states.description: The track before the thumb is filled with the accent, from the theme's tint.

appearance: System appearance in every theme; only the filled track comes from Monarch, through the tint.
platformNotes: The web ships its own Slider with marks under the track, a value shown at the end and a large step for Page Up and Page Down. The system Slider has no marks: show the value in a Text beside it, and use minimumValueLabel and maximumValueLabel for the ends. onEditingChanged(false) is the counterpart of the web's onValueCommit. Android themes the Material 3 Slider.
accessibility: System behaviour: an adjustable element whose value is read as a percentage of the range; swiping up or down changes it.
The label passed to the Slider is not drawn on iOS but is the spoken name, so always give one.
Set accessibilityValue when a percentage is not the meaningful reading, for example "5 seats".
edgeCases: Without a step the value is continuous; round it before showing it.
The thumb is the system's and does not change with Dynamic Type.
